## Disposable runtime contract

The harness builds a fresh acceptance derivative of the unchanged production image. It runs the actual worker entrypoint under `NODE_ENV=production`, UID 10001, a read-only root filesystem and no added capabilities. The existing packaged client still prepares real platform PostgreSQL, an isolated product file fixture and retention sentinels, then executes empty-environment reconciliation and a signed read operation whose real activity must refuse its missing target. It supplies no replacement activity, caller authority boolean, cloud credential or default API startup.

Temporal uses official `temporalio/server:1.32.0` and matching `temporalio/admin-tools:1.32.0`, pinned by multiarch digests in the harness. Admin tools create and migrate separate `temporal` and `temporal_visibility` databases on the new owned PostgreSQL instance. The platform ledger remains in `zenith_packaged`. A whole PostgreSQL pause therefore affects Temporal persistence too; that outage is not proof of independently isolated stores. A separate bounded lock on the platform schema table tests the worker prerequisite alone.

The server loads the committed YAML using its supported `temporal-server --config-file … start` entrypoint. Both frontend and internode require client authentication, verify the private CA, and use the fixed `temporal` DNS SAN. The internode/server leaf has serverAuth and clientAuth usage, as required for Temporal's service clients. The external client leaf has clientAuth usage. HTTP and host-published ports are disabled. This is the real server's TLS, with no authenticated proxy or verification bypass.

The harness mints short-lived CA/server/client material with supported OpenSSL 3 or LibreSSL 3 in private scratch outside the source tree. Scratch is owned by the invoking UID and mode 0700; generated files are regular, bounded, owner checked and mode 0600. Leaf/private-key matching, CA signatures, purpose and server SAN are checked. CA private keys remain on the host and are deleted with scratch. A short-lived, network-disabled initializer copies only fixed files into new labeled volumes and uses CHOWN only there. Server files are owned by UID 1000; worker files by UID 10001; their private directories are mode 0700. Server and worker subsequently mount separate credential volumes read-only. There are no host directory, socket, PID namespace or device mounts.

An image-local client uses the actual installed SDK and a read-only implementation of the committed encrypted payload wire format. It cannot encode/start an operation or install an activity. It confirms real client authentication, refusal without a client certificate and refusal with an untrusted leaf, and refusal with an incorrect server name, with valid-client controls before and after. It creates one explicit run namespace and registers only the typed `ZenithScheduleOwner` Keyword attribute as an operator fixture action. The worker gets the fixed `zenith-execution` task queue, concurrency 1 and explicit schedule `provision` permission. Normal deployment pollers must not inherit these fixture provisioning rights.

**Namespace authorization remains unproved.** This isolated server requires a trusted certificate but has no namespace authorizer. The owned CA is confined to this disposable instance; it is not a production namespace role or permission configuration.

## Prepared checks and honest result scope

The harness requires all five actual readiness checks, including current reconciliation, and verifies ownership, encrypted input, current run identity and a successful fresh schedule result. It does not equate an action counter, deferred result or old successful pass with current observation. It prepares six exact exit 1/non-OOM startup refusals: missing schema, invalid secret, invalid signer, plaintext Temporal, absent explicit namespace and unsupported sweep routing.

The platform-schema outage holds a real PostgreSQL lock. A fresh third observer must see the exact schema-read waiter, exact blocker application/query and `pg_blocking_pids` relationship with three distinct PIDs. The pass must report deferred and readiness 503 while the schedule stays unpaused; after the bounded blocker exits, a different successful run must restore observation. Dependency pauses retain liveness while revoking readiness, and recovery requires a different completed run. Restarting the owned server must retain its SQL-backed schedule and produce a fresh pass. An explicit operator pause must revoke reconciliation readiness; only an explicit operator unpause resumes it.

The SIGTERM check currently drains an **idle** real worker with exit 0 and secret-free lifecycle logs. It does not establish cancellation or completion of an accepted provider mutation, provider deletion, cleanup quiescence or an in-flight cloud activity. The operation remains an expected no-target read refusal, not a successful cloud deployment. Product identity uses the current local file fixture, not live Supabase/PostgREST/browser authentication. Production HA, Temporal Cloud, production namespace permissions and native AMD64 remain external gaps. AMD64 emulation is labeled separately from native execution.

The safety suite adds source/scalar admission models and one real private-directory permission refusal. Those tests never start Docker or Temporal and cannot prove the generated certificates, server parser, syscall custody, PostgreSQL waiter or actual SDK transport. All those proofs require a fresh runtime attempt; an earlier successful artifact must not rescue a failed current attempt.

## Root integration and runtime prerequisites

Use the existing private `run_packaged_storage.py`/`run_packaged.py` wrapper contract. Before runtime, root must add the pinned server and admin-tools references to its baseline-aware `KNOWN_IMAGES` cleanup list. It must retain its run-owned builder/cache removal, exact image-ID baseline, and deletion only of newly pulled images with no remaining references. The harness observes the supplied local docker-container builder identity, pinned BuildKit image and 4 GiB bound; that observation does not prove who created it. The independent wrapper creation/cleanup receipt is mandatory. Never use a default builder or global prune.

Keep at least 12 GiB free before launch and monitor the 8 GiB reserve during the single workload. Official registry metadata reports approximately 141 MiB compressed for ARM64 server+admin images, or 152 MiB for AMD64; unpacked images, build cache and database growth are unmeasured. Reevaluate actual free disk and memory before any pull. The server is bounded to 1 GiB, PostgreSQL 256 MiB and each worker/client 1.5 GiB; installer/schema clients use 128 MiB. The external builder has its separate4 GiB bound during build. No second heavy workload may overlap.

Root must integrate the reviewed worker/scheduler/current-role/registry/compiler corrections, compile/lint and run the affected safety suite, then execute the harness from a clean exact source through that wrapper. The runtime source inventory binds all copied inputs before/after build plus the harness/config hashes; it remains a live-context capture rather than an immutable build-context claim. Every created container, volume, network, acceptance image and private input must have verified cleanup. The wrapper must independently prove owned builder/cache and newly pulled dependency image absence. Failed setup, failed operation, missing evidence or incomplete cleanup means the attempt failed.

Other paths are untouched: production worker/security guards, Dockerfile, packaged client, shared codec/controller/history, default API, migration registry, canonical gate manifest and requirement ledger. Root owns wrapper pin updates, production imports, per-architecture execution, publication and any navigation/metadata wiring. Do not close the full requirements from these prepared checks.

Existing fixed refusal phases remain admitted. Safety regressions model the diagnostic projection and a refused tool invocation; they do not run cryptography, Docker or Temporal. The waiter rejection table also preserves its five intended array inputs through explicit named rows instead of Vitest spreading them into callback arguments.

## CHOWN-only volume initializer correction

Preserve both failed ARM64 attempts, `operations-packaged-arm64-tls-r1-20261003-*` and `operations-packaged-arm64-tls-diagnostics-r1-20261003-*`. Neither started a server or recorded a passed check. Their generic `acceptance-client` cleanup role can describe the credential initializer; it does not prove that the initializer was absent. The second attempt still lacked a fixed crypto subphase. Root then executed the exact original initializer body on native ARM64 with the same CHOWN-only, network-none, read-only, no-host-mount constraints and observed EPERM. The separate kernel receipt is `operations-initializer-permission-proof-r2-20261004/receipt.json`; owned container, volumes and new image cleanup completed. This confirms the initializer permission defect, not packaged startup acceptance.

The corrected initializer sets permissions while it owns each inode, then transfers ownership. [Linux capabilities](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/capabilities.7.html) distinguish CHOWN from FOWNER; [chmod](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/chmod.2.html) requires ownership or FOWNER. No capability is added. The fixed body exported by `packagedVolumeCustodySource()` is the body executed by the harness and available to root's independent kernel probe. It opens only the nine fixed files and two volume parents with no-follow descriptors, validates original root ownership and bounded regular files before mutation, and rechecks descriptor/name/device/inode/owner/group/mode/size/link metadata plus exact parent entries before each change. It retains descriptors to verify final file metadata after transferring a private parent, since CHOWN-only root cannot traverse the target-owned 0700 directory. Success requires the fixed marker; partial errors refuse without compensation, close descriptors and leave cleanup to the existing owned-volume removal.

The allowlisted diagnostics now also identify initializer start, server/client copy, custody and stop. Raw output, errors, paths and certificate material remain excluded. Added tests execute this same program against explicit filesystem permission ports, covering ordering, both parent identities, unexpected or substituted entries and partial failure. These are modeled filesystem checks, not kernel, certificate, Docker or Temporal proof. Crypto, target UIDs, TLS configuration, read-only/network restrictions, build order and cleanup remain unchanged. Root must independently review, compile/run the affected suite, execute the exact corrected body on the isolated Linux kernel, and repeat the fresh source-bound ARM64 package attempt. Native AMD64, in-flight effect handling and full production acceptance remain open.
